newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria awards $320 mln gas contract.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria awards $320 mln gas contract.

text.p: The Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria said on Monday it had awarded a $320 million contract to an international consortium to build a gas plant that would reduce gas flaring in its operations.
The contract was awarded to the Japan Gasoline Company (JGC) and Italy's Saipem consortium to build the plant at Shell's Soku oil field in the southeastern Rivers state, it said in a statement.

"The project is one of a series of initiatives planned by Shell on behalf of its joint venture partners (state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp) NNPC, Elf and Agip to end unnecessary gas flaring in the company's operations as soon as possible," it said.

Shell, which pumps about half Nigeria's nearly two million barrels per day of crude oil, has been under attack from environmental campaigners over its operations in Nigeria since last November when nine minority rights activists from the oil-producing Ogoniland were hanged for murder.
The activists, among them author Ken Saro-Wiwa, accused Shell of polluting the environment.

Most Nigerian gas is curerently flared in the process of producing crude oil. A $4 billion Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) plant is being built in Bonny, Rivers state to gather and export gas from 1999 and Shell is technical leader of the LNG project.
Shell is contracted to supply gas processed at the new plant in Soku to the LNG.

"The problem of gas flaring is not something Shell can address on its own," Shell Nigeria managing director Brian Anderson said, adding Nigeria must provide fiscal incentives in order to utilise its gas reserves and end wasteful flaring.

The Soku plant is part of a complex of gas facilities that will gather gas from three Shell oil fields and deliver an average of 450 million standard cubic feet a day (scf/d) of gas of which nearly half will come from the company's flare lines.

Shell said its Nigerian joint venture was aiming to develop two other projects -- Odidi and Alscon -- and the three would collect more than 380 million scf/d from flare lines, more than a thrid of the gas currently flared by the company.
Odidi, which is being designed by a British firm, is aimed at collecting gas flared at the Odidi oil field and to supply 80 million scf/d of associated gas to the Nigerian Gas Company.
Another 100 million scf/d of Shell's associated gas will be diverted from the flares to fuel a new aluminium plant being built at Ikot Abasi by the Aluminium Smelter Company (ALSCON).
